title: Bytes with a lone UTF-8 continuation byte inside portName must be refused as invalid-utf8
notes: source: WV-PORT-API-STALL-SUSPENDED-01, mutation: one lone continuation byte 0x80 inserted at byte offset 135 (0-based), between `in` and `let` of the portName value — `"in` 0x80 `let"` — giving 201 bytes that are not valid UTF-8; no `encoded.utf8` because the bytes are not text. Every other byte is the seed's, so after U+FFFD substitution the text is still a well-formed frame with the seed's known ids: the only thing standing between these bytes and a returned invocation is UTF-8 validation, which isolates [WIR1-I07]'s UTF-8 clause from its malformed-JSON clause (ncz.6-D5). Normative: [WIR1-I07] says such bytes SHALL be rejected, so `expect.reject` is `invalid-utf8` for every conforming implementation. The reference JVM codec at codecVersion 2 does NOT reject: WireCodec.decodeFrame calls bytes.decodeToString() (= String(bytes, UTF_8)), which substitutes U+FFFD and returns an invocation whose portName is `in\uFFFDlet` (observed 2026-09-25 through the full codec). `expect.observed: accepted-with-substitution` records that divergence and the JVM driver asserts it, pinned-because-current ([WIR1-C16]) — a codec fix turns this vector red, the signal to drop `observed`. Ledger: wire/corpus/NONDETERMINISM.md §Findings. Fix owned by bug computenet-ezw1d.
